decision: client-event rate limiter is in memory, 10 per rolling second per socket
why: hibernation resets it, which the unit brief accepts; persisting timestamps would write to storage on every client event for a limit Pusher resets anyway

decision: park the /events encrypted-channel inconsistency for U5
why: batch rejects private-encrypted-* but the single publish route still accepts it; no subscriber can exist because subscribe rejects, so this is consistency work, not a leak

decision: SQLite-backed Durable Objects and no nodejs_compat
why: free-plan deployments need SQLite-backed DOs; the runtime has no node builtins, and every gate plus the 18-check harness passes without the flag
evidence: wrangler.jsonc, worker-configuration.d.ts, pnpm build, pnpm compat

decision: cache-* stays a plain public channel
why: the server has no cache state, but accepting the name lets live events flow and the README says cache is unsupported; rejecting would add a new error without implementing the feature
evidence: README support matrix, live cache-smoke subscribe

decision: treat an empty filter_by_prefix as no filter
why: an empty prefix means all channels in Pusher; the shared channel-name schema rejects an empty string, so the route normalizes empty to undefined while still validating non-empty prefixes

decision: 256 KiB HTTP body and 64 KiB WebSocket frame ceilings with the official 1-200 channel charset
why: the signed data paths already cap at 10 KiB but buffered or parsed unbounded input; caps are large enough for a 10-event batch and a presence auth and reject before allocation/parsing

decision: per-channel Channel Durable Object for cache and history
why: one WebSocket can only be owned by AppHub, so channel DOs own durable per-channel state while AppHub keeps live sockets and presence; avoids duplicate presence and shared cache tables

decision: cache TTL is PUSHER_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS, default and maximum 1800
why: Pusher caps cache TTL at 30 minutes; a shorter operator setting is useful for tests and expiry control

decision: history retention is 24 hours and 1000 events per channel
why: self-hosted scope needs bounded SQLite growth; the history API is a depush extension, not Pusher event history

decision: presence-info API reads live AppHub state
why: presence is live connection state; a Channel DO cannot own a socket, and duplicating membership would drift
changing PUSHER_APP_ID must not expose the previous app cache or history; the AppHub is already app-scoped
